UNDERSTAND THE EVIDENCE

Sources, method & limitations

Download methodology ↓

What this tool supports

Shortlist occupations for employer conversations and identify skills to investigate for training curricula. Compare pay, growth and hiring volume before deciding where to do deeper research.

How the data was collected

The statewide Massachusetts Department of Economic Research CSV was downloaded on September 22, 2026. Its occupation codes were matched to O*NET 31.0 national skill importance ratings. Only exact six-digit SOC plus “.00” matches are used.

No survey respondents, names, contact details or personal locations were collected.

Massachusetts DER · projections and wages ↗O*NET 31.0 · occupational skills ↗Prepared occupation dataset · CSV ↓Prepared skills dataset · CSV ↓

Read these measures correctly

Annual openings
Average yearly openings from growth, labor-force exits and occupational transfers over 2024–2034. Not a count of job advertisements.
Growth
Percentage change in employment from 2024 to 2034. The overview combines base and projected employment before calculating the percentage.
Mean annual wage
2025 average annual OES wage reported in the DER file, in US dollars. The overview displays the median of these occupation averages, not the median worker’s pay.
Skill importance
O*NET national ratings on a 1–5 scale. Suppressed ratings are excluded. Collection dates vary by occupation and are retained in the skills CSV.

What the data cannot prove

  • No measured local skills gap: worker skills, training capacity and graduate counts are absent.
  • Forecast uncertainty: projections are estimates, not guaranteed job outcomes.
  • Geographic limits: statewide figures can hide regional differences; skills are national.
  • Coverage: 62 occupations lack an exact O*NET skills match and 19 wage values are unavailable. Totals cover the 634 published occupation rows, which do not sum to the source’s all-occupations total. Missing values remain missing, never zero.
  • Access barriers: entry education is a typical category; licensing, costs and experience can also matter.

Before funding a program

  1. Check the shortlist with local employers, including whether they struggle to hire or retain workers.
  2. Compare relevant graduate output and training capacity using IPEDS or ROAD. Account for migration and multiple career paths.
  3. Review course content, cost, prerequisites and accessibility with training providers.
